outputs.exact_statement: Let $f_1,f_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb D$ be multiplicative, and suppose that at least one satisfies [eq:unp]. For every fixed pair of distinct nonnegative integers $h_1,h_2$, $$\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(n+h_1)f_2(n+h_2)\longrightarrow0 \qquad(N\longrightarrow\infty,\ N\in\mathbb N).$$

Let $f_1,f_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb D$ be multiplicative, with at least one satisfying [eq:unp]. For all fixed integers $a_1,a_2\ge1$ and $b_1,b_2\ge0$ with $a_1b_2-a_2b_1\ne0$, $$\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(a_1n+b_1)f_2(a_2n+b_2) \longrightarrow0.$$
For sufficiently large $X$, $$\frac12SV_*\le S_0\le SV_*.$$

Under the hypotheses of [q:finite-law](#q:finite-law), write $\mathbb E$ for expectation under $\mu$. Suppose $\Phi=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_\alpha}$, where every event has the stated circuit bounds and $\sum_\alpha|c_\alpha|\le\exp(C L^5)$ for a fixed constant $C$. Then, for sufficiently large $L$, $$\label{q:scalar-comparison}
                 |\mathbb E_I\Phi-\mathbb E\Phi|\le e^{-L^9}.$$ This also applies to the sum of errors for a family of such expansions when the same bound holds for their total absolute coefficient sum.

With the parameters and prime supplies fixed above, for every sufficiently large real $X$ one has $$\label{q:center-estimate}
 \left|\sum_j C_j-S_0F(X)\right|
 \ll_{h,l}SV_*\left(
   \eta+X^{-1}+\eta^{-1}2^JL^{-1/20}\right).$$

Let $L$ be sufficiently large, let $h\ge1$ be an integer, and suppose $$\tfrac12\exp(L^{0.995})\le D\le\exp(2L).$$ Let $\mathcal Z\subset[D,2D)$ consist of integers with no prime factor at most $\exp(L^{0.99})$. For $$B(\theta)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\frac{\mathrm e(hz\theta)}z
 \qquad(\theta\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)$$ one has, with absolute implied constants, $$\label{q:rough-bounds}
 \|B\|_\infty\ll L^{-0.99},\qquad
 \int_0^1|B(\theta)|^4\,d\theta\ll D^{-1}L^{-3.96}.$$

For every $d\in\mathcal D$ and the bin width $\eta=e^{-J}$, $$\label{q:padding-square}
 \mathbb E^*\sum_j\rho_j(n,d)^2\ll_{h,l}L^{-1}.$$ The constant is independent of $d$, $W$, and the location of the bins.

Consider at most $R\le4L$ signed steps together with additional records having at most $L^{O(1)}$ choices per prime slot. Then the number of equality patterns and such records is at most $\exp(O(R\log^2L))$. With one reciprocal for every distinct prime, the sum over their numerical values has the same bound, also after multiplication by $Lu(q_i)$ for each step.*

*Suppose, with the padding values fixed, that a recorded relation in the tuple primes is $$az+c\equiv0\pmod p,\qquad a\not\equiv0\pmod p,$$ where $a,c,p$ are independent of the selected prime variable $z$. Its reciprocal sum costs at most $(1+L)/H_0$ in place of an unrestricted prime sum. Such savings multiply when selected variables are ordered so that each relation uses only its own variable, earlier selected variables, and nonselected variables.

The event in [q:prohibited](#q:prohibited) is translation covariant and satisfies $$\mathbb P(n\in\mathcal B_j)
 \le\exp\bigl(-\tfrac12L^{1-\delta}\bigr).$$ As a function of the residue equalities it has a Boolean circuit of depth two and size at most $\exp(L^3)$ for sufficiently large $L$.
The total contribution to the moment majorant from designated terms with $U>L^{1/50}$ is at most $\exp(-L^{1+\delta})$.

Let $\mathscr P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathscr P$ with $\max_{p\in\mathscr P}\mu(p)\le\alpha$. Let $r\ge1$, let $B\in M_r(\mathbb Z)$ be nonsingular over $\mathbb R$, and let $f:\mathscr P^r\to\mathbb Z^r$ be any function. Suppose that $M\ge2$ and $$\left|(B(y-y'))_i\right|\le M
 \quad\text{for all }y,y'\in\mathscr P^r\text{ and }1\le i\le r.$$ If the $2r$ coordinates of $c,y\in\mathscr P^r$ are independent with law $\mu$, then $$\label{q:rank-probability-bound}
 \mathbb P\bigl(c_i\mid(By+f(c))_i\text{ for every }i\bigr)
 \le \left[\alpha(1+d_M)\right]^{r/2},
 \qquad d_M=\left\lfloor\frac{\log M}{\log2}\right\rfloor.$$

In the sum of the nonnegative majorants from [q:mixed-difference](#q:mixed-difference), the total contribution of words having a column with $r$ jointly independent pairs [q:rank-pair] is $$O\left(\exp(-c_0 L^{203/200})\right)$$ for some absolute $c_0>0$ and sufficiently large $L$. The bound includes the external dimension factors in the trace expansion and is uniform in the bin. The threshold may depend on the fixed parameters $W,h,l$.

Fix a numerical main word with singleton set $\mathcal U$, where $S_1=|\mathcal U|>L^{1/4}$, and fix a draw of the residue coordinates. If $\Delta G\ne0$, then some hybrid contains $T$ positive witnesses attached at main departures, each of length at most $s$, with distinct marked primes $y_1,\ldots,y_T\in\mathcal U$. The prime $y_j$ occurs in witness $j$ and in none of the other $T-1$ witnesses. The combined length of the main word and these witnesses is at most $4L$.

Let $E_1,\ldots,E_m$ be a minimal prohibited word. For every $P$ label $y$ in this word, either $y$ is active or there are an active label $z$ and a step $i$ containing $z$ such that $$\label{q:active-prefix} \sum_{\substack{a[q:active-definition] with contiguous intervals.

For a fixed bin, the total contribution to the absolute majorants in [q:mixed-difference](#q:mixed-difference) from main words with $S_1>L^{1/4}$, including the external factor $|\mathcal D|^2M$ in the trace expansion, is at most $$\exp(-L^{21/20})$$ for sufficiently large $L$, with the fixed parameters held fixed.
In each such block, the occurrences of every column prime form an interval of consecutive positions. No nonempty subinterval of the block has total displacement zero.

Suppose that $$S_1\le L^{1/4},\qquad U\le L^{1/50},\qquad r=\lfloor L^{1/50}\rfloor,$$ and that, in every column, there are no $r$ pairs [q:rank-pair] whose $2r$ vectors are jointly independent. Consider lit-consistent terms of [q:mixed-difference](#q:mixed-difference) with a nonzero integrand. The equality patterns that can occur in any one column belong to a set of cardinality at most $\exp(Ck)$, for an absolute constant $C$. This set can be chosen independently of all numerical coefficients and padding choices. Consequently there are at most $\exp(CJk)$ combined column patterns.

Let $N\ge1$ and let $B_1,\ldots,B_N$ be self-adjoint operators on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and let $P$ be an orthogonal projection on $\mathcal H$. Define an operator $\mathscr B$ on $\mathcal H^N$ by $$\mathscr B_{i,j}=\mathbf 1_{i\ne j}B_j.$$ Suppose $a,b\ge0$, $\|B_i\|\le a$ for every $i$, and $$\sum_{i=1}^N\|B_i v\|^2\le b^2\|v\|^2
 \qquad(v=Pv).$$ Writing $\rho(\mathscr B)$ for its spectral radius, one has $$\label{q:noncommuting-bound}
 \left\|P\left(\sum_{i=1}^N B_i\right)P\right\|
 \le 3\max\{a,b,\rho(\mathscr B)\}.$$

For every bin $j$ and all sufficiently large $X$, $$\label{q:bin-estimate} |C_j^\circ|\ll \frac{S K(C_3\sqrt W)^J}{L}+e^{-L}.$$ The threshold may depend on the fixed $h,l,W$, while $C_3$ is the absolute constant in [q:C3-choice].
Let $f\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb C$ be multiplicative and $|f|\le1$. If $$\sum_p\frac{1-|f(p)|}{p}=\infty,$$ then $N^{-1}\sum_{n\le N}|f(n)|\to0$.

Let $f_1,f_2\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb C$ be $1$-bounded multiplicative functions satisfying [eq:analytic-finite-defects] and $f_1(1)=f_2(1)=1$. Fix $1<\tau<2$. There are constants $C_0\ge1$ and $c>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large $B$, one can choose $1\le H\le\exp(C_0B)$ and a family $\mathcal D$ of squarefree $\mathcal S$-products satisfying $$\begin{gathered} H1,\qquad \omega(d)\le J=\lceil C_0\log B\rceil, \qquad |f_1(d)f_2(d)|\ge\tfrac12, \label{eq:raw-selected-divisors}\\ \sum_{d\in\mathcal D}\frac{A^{\omega_C(d)}}d \ge c\frac{L_0}{B}. \label{eq:raw-bin-mass} \end{gathered}$$ The constants are independent of $B$ and of the long averaging variable.

Fix $C_0\ge1$, $1<\tau<2$, and an integer $h\ge1$. Let $P_0=\exp(B^{1-\varepsilon})$, where $\varepsilon=10^{-4}$, and suppose $P_0/\tau\le M\le\exp(C_0B)$. If $|c_w|\le1$ and $c_w=0$ unless $w\in(M,\tau M]$ is $P_0$-rough, then, for all sufficiently large $B$, $$\begin{aligned}
 \|Q_M\|_\infty&\ll B^{-1+\varepsilon}\log B,
 \label{eq:rough-sup}\\
 \int_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}|Q_M(\alpha)|^4\,d\alpha
 &\ll M^{-1}B^{-4+4\varepsilon}(\log B)^6.
 \label{eq:rough-fourth}
\end{aligned}$$ The constants are uniform in $M$ and the coefficients.
If a specification qualifies, a primitive specification using only its prime support qualifies at one of its path vertices, along a contiguous subpath in one of the two orientations.
The set $Y$ satisfies [eq:deleted-density].

For sufficiently large $B$, let a primitive specification have edge labels $e_1,\ldots,e_m$, extra prime $p$, and suffix ending at $m$. Then the following statements hold.*

1.  *For every edge prime $q$, the indices $i$ with $q\mid e_i$ form an interval of consecutive indices.*

2.  *Let $b$ be the first index of the final maximal constant block $e_b=\cdots=e_m$. Then $b>1$, the signs on this block are constant, and there exists $r\mid e_b$ with $r\nmid e_{b-1}$. Every such $r$ occurs only in the constant tail. In the specified suffix displacement, its coefficient as a prime variable is nonzero modulo $p$. This coefficient assertion holds for any edge prime whose occurrences are confined to that tail.*

3.  *If $q$ occurs before $b$ and $r$ is as in the preceding part, the coefficient of $q$ in $z_{b-1}-z_0$ is nonzero modulo $r$.*

*Coefficients here are obtained by fixing all other distinct prime values; squarefreeness makes each displacement linear in the prime being varied.

In the positive count of [lem:crude-count](#lem:crude-count), suppose every configuration under consideration supplies at least $B^{2\varepsilon}$ distinct prime variables $q_1,\ldots,q_k$ and tests with the following properties. Test $j$ uses only $q_j$, the earlier variables $q_1,\ldots,q_{j-1}$, and nonselected variables, and is either*

1.  *$q_j\mid D_j$, where $D_j\ne0$ is independent of $q_j$ and $\log(|D_j|+2)=O(B\log B)$; or*

2.  *$a_jq_j+c_j\equiv0\pmod{r_j}$, where $a_j,c_j,r_j$ are independent of $q_j$, $r_j$ is an earlier or nonselected prime variable, and $a_j\not\equiv0\pmod{r_j}$.*


*Assume the choices of tests and their order have $\exp(O(B\log^2B))$ descriptions. Then their total absolute contribution, also allowing the attached specifications in [lem:crude-count](#lem:crude-count), is $$\label{eq:negligible-constraints}
 O\bigl(\exp(-B^{1+\varepsilon/2})\bigr).$$ The description bound applies in particular when each test uses a bounded number of displacements along contiguous line or attached paths, or along paths in a recorded tree of line steps, together with one common specified integer offset of size $O(\ell H)$.

For each closed line there is a predicate $R_{\boldsymbol d}(n_{\mathcal F})\in\{0,1\}$ with the following properties. Whenever it equals one:*

1.  *all core line occurrences are lit; no primitive specification with support contained in $\mathcal F$ qualifies at a trace vertex; and fewer than $t_0$ repeated center occurrences are unlit;*

2.  *every fixed tree prime has $O(B^\rho)$ active components; fewer than $B^{1-2\rho}$ fixed tree primes have more than one active component;*

3.  *fewer than $B^{1-2\rho}$ nonfixed tree primes are corrupted.*


*The implicit constant is uniform in the line. Moreover, $$\label{eq:retained-line-error}
 \sum_{\boldsymbol d}
  \mathbb E\left[|K_{\boldsymbol d}(n)|
       \prod_{j=0}^{\ell}\mathbf 1_Y(n+b_j)
       (1-R_{\boldsymbol d}(n_{\mathcal F}))\right]
 \ll \exp(-B^{1+\varepsilon/2}).$$ The same exceptional estimates used in this proof remain valid after adding the qualification indicators of at most $2t_0$ specifications and summing their recorded data, for the classes discarded by an arithmetic saving. Configurations excluded because of a fixed forbidden specification instead vanish with the original $Y$ factors.
Let a finite forest carry a finite family of nonempty edge paths. If the family has no $t$ pairwise edge-disjoint paths, some set of fewer than $2t$ edges meets every path in the family.

Except for configurations of zero contribution in [eq:retained-line-error] or total absolute contribution $O(\exp(-B^{1+\varepsilon/2}))$, one can cut $O(t_0)$ edges of the first-visit tree and cover the resulting forest by $O(B^\rho)$ connected blocks of diameter at most $L$. The blocks cover every remaining edge and every vertex of the original tree. In each block, the active set of every fixed tree prime is connected or empty. Consequently each fixed tree prime has $O(B^\rho)$ whole-tree active components.

Let two connected blocks of a tree and $m$ distinct prime indices $p$ be given. For each index let $V_p$ be a vertex subset, and let $A_p^j$ be its intersection with block $j$. Suppose these intersections are nonempty and connected. Edges have labels containing at most $J$ prime factors. In either block, an edge has both endpoints in $A_p^j$ if and only if its label contains $p$. Assume also that $A_p^1$ and $A_p^2$ lie in distinct components of the subgraph induced by $V_p$ in the whole tree.*

*There are roots $c_j$ in block $j$, a set of $\gg m^{1/8}/(2J+1)$ retained indices, and an order on those indices with the following property. If $x_p^j$ is the nearest vertex of $A_p^j$ to $c_j$, both paths from $c_j$ to $x_p^j$ avoid $p$, and any retained prime label on either path occurs earlier in the order. The two representatives $x_p^1,x_p^2$ are distinct.

Among the configurations retained by [lem:activity-blocks](#lem:activity-blocks), those with at least $B^{1-2\rho}$ fixed tree primes having multiple active components have total absolute contribution $O(\exp(-B^{1+\varepsilon/2}))$.
Lines having at least $B^{1-2\rho}$ corrupted nonfixed tree primes have total absolute contribution $O(\exp(-B^{1+\varepsilon/2}))$.

Let $\boldsymbol d$ be a numerical closed line, and let $\mathcal F$ contain its core prime labels and all labels occurring at least twice on the line. Suppose $t_0$ primitive specifications attached at line vertices qualify simultaneously. Suppose that each has a prime outside $\mathcal F$ absent from every other specification in this family. For sufficiently large $B$, their numerical labels satisfy a triangular system on at least $B^{2\varepsilon}$ distinct selected prime variables of the kind in [lem:triangular-saving](#lem:triangular-saving). Each constraint uses one intrinsic suffix displacement, or the difference of two witness prefixes and a line segment. Its nonzero expressions have logarithmic size $O(B\log B)$ even when numerical label-size restrictions are dropped.

For every finite rooted tree and every $A_a>0$ with $\beta_a=(1+A_a)^{-1}$, $$\label{eq:subtree-identity}
 \sum_{Q:\,|E(Q)|\ge1}u_a(Q)=S_a(\mathscr T)\le |V(\mathscr T)|.$$

For retained data, these records have the following properties.*

1.  *They recover every tree-edge label. Together with the topology and the list data they consequently recover the full line and list.*

2.  *The total number of tagged tokens and list prime slots is at most $N_{\mathrm{exc}}$, for sufficiently large $B$.*

3.  *An untagged fixed center prime cannot have a single good edge as its token.

For sufficiently large $B$, the total conditional main term supplied by [prop:cylinder-reduction](#prop:cylinder-reduction), including its $\exp(O(M_0\log B))$ prefactor, is at most $B^{-(1+2c_*)\ell}$.

Let $f,G\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb D$ be multiplicative, let $\psi$ be a fixed Dirichlet character, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes. If $G(p)=f(p)\psi(p)$ for every $p\notin S$, then for every Dirichlet character $\chi$, every real $t$, and every $X\ge2$, $$\left|D(G,\chi n^{it};X)^2
       -D(f,(\chi\overline\psi)n^{it};X)^2\right|
 \le 2\sum_{p\in S}\frac1p.
 \label{eq:affine-stability}$$ Thus uniform nonpretentiousness of $f$ implies that of $G$. Complex conjugation also preserves uniform nonpretentiousness.

For every fixed Dirichlet character $\chi$, $$\inf_{|t|\le X}D(\lambda,\chi n^{it};X)
 \ge \frac14\sqrt{\log\log X}-O_\chi(1)
 \qquad(X\ge100).
 \label{eq:affine-liouville-unp}$$ In particular, $\lambda$ is uniformly nonpretentious.
